title: Go SDK: robust stream recovery for interrupted reads, cancellation races, and retry ergonomics
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Current Go SDK streaming helpers do not handle mid-stream interruptions and context deadline races cleanly. Customers see partial payloads, confusing errors, and unexpected reconnect behavior when their request context times out while the SDK is in the middle of assembling chunks. Scope: Implement a StreamClient API that makes caller intent explicit (Cancel vs ShortRead vs Resume), propagates per-operation deadlines, coordinates client-side retries/backoff for interrupted reads, and provides clear errors for terminal vs transient failures. Goals: (1) No lost goroutine leaks during cancel/reconnect, (2) deterministic error types so callers can decide whether to retry, (3) ergonomic examples for common patterns (single-request with timeout, long-lived chat with per-message deadlines, resumable stream for large responses). Acceptance criteria: - New API available in go-sdk vX.Y with examples - Tests cover cancellation race, context-with-deadline overlapping read, and retry backoff behavior - No regression on existing streaming benchmarks - Docs and example snippets added to README and console docs
tasks: Design StreamClient interface and error taxonomy (transient vs terminal)
Implement per-read deadline propagation: separate operation timeout from overall request timeout
Add client-side reconnect with exponential backoff and idempotency hints for resume-able endpoints
Ensure context cancellation cancels underlying HTTP/gRPC request and unblocks read loops
Add unit/integration tests for race conditions and metrics (open goroutines, open connections)
Write examples: single-call with timeout, long-lived chat with per-message deadline, resumable stream usage
comments: 2026-02-11 - Ava Chen: Kickoff discussion notes: opt to treat mid-stream EOF caused by transient connection drop as RetriableStreamError when server signals resume token present. We should avoid automatically retrying if the caller explicitly canceled the context.

2026-02-16 - Diego Marquez: Spike completed with prototype StreamClient.ReadLoop() that separates read deadlines using ctx = context.WithTimeout(parentCtx, perReadTimeout). Prototype shows no goroutine leaks in local sim; pushing PR next.

2026-02-18 - Priya Natarajan (PM): UX note: Examples must show how to compose per-message timeouts in chat use case. Add a short snippet to docs explaining trade-offs between per-read timeouts and whole-request timeouts.

2026-02-20 - Code Review (Liam O'Connor): Requested changes: - Return typed errors: ErrStreamCanceled, ErrStreamTimeout, ErrStreamResumable, ErrStreamTerminal. - Add metrics for retry_count and last_resume_token. - Ensure Resume() only attempted once per identified resumable error to avoid "thundering" retries.

2026-02-24 - Diego Marquez: Addressed review comments, added Metrics (stream_retries_total, stream_resume_token) and a simple backoff util. Push PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/412

2026-02-26 - QA (Maya Singh): Integration test flake observed when per-read timeout is very small (<50ms) — test adapted to use per-read timeout + jitter in test harness. Also verified no leaking goroutines under 1k parallel simulated streams.
2026-03-01 - Ava Chen: Merged docs into master, added example snippets and updated CHANGELOG. Follow-up: evaluate default per-read timeout value and consider making it configurable via SDK Options.
